Morwen Coombe.narrative: I keep the dairy and work the Lakemead strips, same as my mother did, though the meadow was never ours to hold. Jem pays Nell Sedge rent in grain and cheese, and this year the grain is thin and the cheese is carrying us. Elmwick men have pulled our fence down twice, and I mend it with Jem and say nothing, because Rowan Wray is still my friend and I will not make her choose. I count what we owe every night before I sleep.
values: not letting the quarrel poison old friendships
goals: make up the grain rent with cheese and labour before Nell Sedge loses patience
keep the fence standing through the winter
keep her friendship with Rowan Wray despite Elmwick and Reedmoor
see Cedda safe and not walking roads with a pedlar's packs
learn to set a hard cheese that keeps through winter so the dairy carries us when grain is thin
mend the fence well enough that it stands a whole season without Jem's help

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He carries the worry with me, and he mends the fence without complaining.

relations.name: Cedda Coombe
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is quick and brave and I do not want her on the east road with a pedlar.

relations.name: Osric Coombe
relations.label: son
relations.note: He follows the goats and is afraid of the reeds; I keep him close.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: She has not pressed us, but the tally is short and she holds the meadow.

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: I carry cheese to her table and she does not ask too many questions.

relations.name: Rowan Wray
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Elmwick or not, she is my friend, and I will not let this quarrel take her.

relations.name: Rill Fenlake
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She has a right to be angry about her nets, but I miss the Elmwick fish.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He brings fish and stories, and I am not ready to let Cedda go with him.

relations.name: Tibbott Coombe
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He keeps the bees and the old tally, and he remembers when the meadow was common.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: quarrel
relations.note: His men pulled our fence down twice; I will not forget it.

relations.name: Eadric Sedge
relations.label: landlord's brother
relations.note: He fishes the reed beds for Nell and grumbles that we owe her grain; I keep my head down and my cheese ready when he comes by.

memories.gist: The first time Elmwick men pulled the fence down, Jem and I rebuilt it in the rain while Cedda held the posts.
Rowan Wray and I traded cheese and smoked fish at the Ferncross market before the quarrel, and she laughed at my city ways.
The Lean Year came and the meadow grain was thin, and Nell Sedge said nothing about the rent, which was worse than shouting.
Osric was born in the dairy in a hard frost, and Hilda Sedge came with blankets and barley broth.
The second fence-pulling, when the Elmwick men trampled Rill's nets and I found her crying by the lake.

stances.why: The tally is short and Nell has not pressed us; that is a kindness I will not abuse.
It is our living and our dairy, and I will mend the fence as often as they pull it down.
Rowan Wray is not her village's fence-pullers, and I will not lose her over Hob Garrow's temper.
Cedda is too young for the east road, and Osric is afraid of the reeds; I keep them near.
If the grain will not come, the cheese will, and Hilda Sedge pays fair.

Morwen Coombe.secret: She has been selling a little more cheese than Jem knows, and hiding the marks in the thatch against the day Nell takes the meadow back.
pastimes: turning the cheese in the dairy and pressing the curds by hand
sitting with Rowan Wray over a cup when the work is done
walking the meadow edge at dusk to count the goats home
Morwen Coombe.calling: I make the cheese and keep the dairy, and I'd sooner be judged by that than by whose name is on the meadow.

Cedda Coombe.narrative: I help with the goats and the fence, and I am not afraid of the Elmwick men, only of what they do to the fence. Thistle Mossfoot comes through the meadow with his packs and tells me about Fernhollow and the giants' shelf, and I have already told Thea Wray I am going to see it. Mother says I am too young, but I am eleven and I can walk.
goals: walk a stretch of the east road with Thistle Mossfoot's packs
see Fernhollow and the giants' shelf
keep the goats from straying into the reeds
learn the east road's turns well enough to walk a stretch of it with Thistle's packs
save up something worth trading so she can pay her own way to Fernhollow

relations.name: Morwen Coombe
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She says I am too young for the road, but she has not forbidden it outright.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: father
relations.note: He half-promised I could walk with Thistle when the packs are light.

relations.name: Osric Coombe
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He is afraid of the reeds; I hold his hand at the meadow edge.

relations.name: Thea Wray
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is Elmwick, but she is my friend, and I told her I am going to Fernhollow.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He tells the best stories of the hollow and the giants' shelf.

relations.name: Merewyn Sedge
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play at the meadow edge and she is not afraid of the reeds like Osric.

relations.name: Tibbott Coombe
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: He keeps the bees and the rent tally and tells me how the meadow was grazed by Elmwick and Reedmoor both, long before it was let; I sit with him when the fence wants mending.

memories.gist: The Elmwick men came and pulled the fence down, and I hid behind the goat shed until they were gone.
Thistle Mossfoot opened his pack and showed me a fernhollow salve and a fish smoked in the east, and I decided I would go.
I told Thea Wray I was going to see Fernhollow, and she said she would come if her father let her.
Helping Jem mend the fence the second time, holding the posts straight while he hammered.

stances.why: Thistle's stories are better than anything in the meadow, and I am not a baby.
The goats and the fence are ours, and I am old enough to help.
Thea Wray did not pull our fence down, and I will not stop being her friend.

pastimes: running the goats out to the meadow edge and back
listening to Thistle Mossfoot's stories of Fernhollow and the giants' shelf
playing fence-and-gate games with Thea Wray and Merewyn Sedge
Cedda Coombe.calling: I want to walk the roads and see every place on the island, and one day carry a pedlar's packs of my own.

Osric Coombe.narrative: I play at the meadow edge and follow the goats, and I do not like the deep reeds where the water is dark. When the Elmwick men shouted, I hid in the house. I like it when Merewyn Sedge comes to play.
goals: stay near the house and the goats
stay close to the house and the goats where it feels safe
play with Merewyn Sedge as often as she comes

relations.name: Morwen Coombe
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps me close and I like that.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: father
relations.note: He carries me on his shoulders past the reeds.

relations.name: Cedda Coombe
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She holds my hand at the meadow edge and tells me not to be afraid.

relations.name: Merewyn Sedge
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She comes to play and is not afraid of the reeds like me.

relations.name: Tibbott Coombe
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: He sits with the bees and lets me watch, and he smells of smoke and honey.

memories.gist: The Elmwick men shouted and pulled the fence down, and I hid behind the house until Jem found me.
Merewyn Sedge and I played at the meadow edge with the goats until the sun went down.

pastimes: chasing the goats around the meadow edge
building little fences and huts out of sticks
Osric Coombe.calling: I like helping with the goats, and when I'm big I want to keep goats too.
